report.summary: Chunk 12 of 12: delete_branch, commit_candidate, has_changes; claims verified.

symbols.name: delete_branch
symbols.note: Deletes a branch, first with -d, then with -D if tip matches proven_tip.

symbols.name: commit_candidate
symbols.note: Stages and commits all changes in an allocated worktree.

symbols.name: has_changes
symbols.note: Returns True if worktree has uncommitted changes via git status --porcelain.

claims.text: ``-d`` is tried first so git's own merged-check applies.
the sha proof (re-taken here, so the branch cannot have moved in between) is what authorises ``-D``.
claims.why: Code retrieves tip via rev-parse and compares to proven_tip before force delete.

claims.text: The force flag is never reached without that proof.
claims.why: Force delete (branch -D) is only executed after the tip check passes; otherwise RuntimeError is raised.

claims.text: Commits all changes in the specified worktree.
claims.why: Code runs git add -A and git commit in the worktree.

claims.text: The path is proven to be an allocated worktree first: a swapped directory would otherwise turn ``git add -A`` + ``git commit`` into a commit of the developer's working tree.
claims.why: The method _require_allocated_worktree is not defined in this chunk; its behaviour cannot be verified.

claims.text: Return whether the candidate worktree differs from its HEAD.
claims.why: Code runs git status --porcelain and returns bool of the output.

observations.what: delete_branch uses 'proven_tip' parameter to authorise force deletion; the docstring explains the logic.
commit_candidate calls _require_allocated_worktree but that method is not defined in this chunk.
has_changes returns bool of git status --porcelain output; empty string is falsy.
